title: Prohibited Emoji 🚫 Meaning: Not Allowed, Banned, Off-Limits
description: The 🚫 prohibited emoji is a red circle with a slash meaning not allowed. See how it sets boundaries, bans things in jokes, and differs from ⛔ and ❌.
summary: The 🚫 prohibited emoji, a red circle with a diagonal slash, means something is forbidden, banned, or unwelcome. People place it before a word to negate it ("🚫 drama"), use it to state rules and boundaries, and deploy it jokingly to outlaw things they dislike.
meaning: 🚫 is the "no" symbol from signs everywhere: no smoking, no parking, no dogs. As an emoji it keeps that function and adds a grammatical trick. Put it in front of almost any word or emoji and it cancels it, so "🚫🧢" means no cap, "🚫 excuses" means none will be accepted, and "🚫📱" means phones away.

This makes it the go-to emoji for rules and boundaries. Group chat admins, event organizers, and community moderators use it in lists of what is not permitted. Individuals use it in bios and captions to draw personal lines, for example "🚫 DMs" or "🚫 negativity," stating plainly what they will not tolerate or respond to.

It also describes self-imposed bans. People post "🚫 sugar for 30 days" or "🚫 texting my ex" when announcing a challenge or a resolution, and gym and wellness accounts use it to label habits to drop. The tone here is determined rather than hostile; the sign is aimed at oneself.

Humor accounts for much of its everyday use. Declaring something "banned" with mock authority, such as Mondays, coriander, or a friend's terrible playlist, is a familiar joke format. Compared with ❌, which merely says no or wrong, 🚫 implies an actual rule has been issued, which is what makes the exaggeration funny.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends use 🚫 to veto plans or lay down playful laws: "🚫 talking about work tonight." It is common in quick refusals too, often next to 🙅. Because it looks like a regulation, sending it in an argument can feel like shutting the conversation down, which is sometimes exactly the intent.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Bios and pinned posts use 🚫 for boundaries such as no reposts, no unsolicited messages, or no minors on adult accounts. Fitness and diet content uses it to list foods or behaviors to avoid. In slang it mostly appears in "no cap" spelled out as 🚫🧢, a way of swearing that something is true.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It suits policy reminders and checklists: "🚫 Do not merge on Fridays" or "🚫 No food in the lab." In status updates it can mark a blocked item, though ⛔ and ❌ are also used. Keep it attached to rules and facts, since pointing it at a person's suggestion feels like a reprimand.

examples.text: New year rules: 🚫 doomscrolling before bed
examples.meaning: The sender is banning a habit for themselves as a resolution.

examples.text: That was the best burger I've ever had 🚫🧢
examples.meaning: "No cap": they are being completely sincere, not exaggerating.

examples.text: 🚫 Spoilers in this chat until Sunday please
examples.meaning: A group rule asking everyone to hold off discussing the plot.
A firm rejection of a person as a romantic option.

examples.text: 🚫 Parking in front of the garage, delivery coming at 9
examples.meaning: A practical notice that a space must be kept clear.

combos.meaning: No cap; slang for "no lie" or "I'm serious."
No phones: a phone-free dinner, a digital detox, or a venue rule.
A strong double refusal, combining the crossed-arms gesture with the ban sign.
Not drinking: sober, on a dry month, or the designated driver.

confusedWith.difference: ⛔ is a solid red disc with a white horizontal bar, the traffic sign for "do not enter." 🚫 is a hollow circle with a diagonal slash and prohibits an activity or thing in general. Use ⛔ for access and 🚫 for behavior.
❌ means no, wrong, or cancelled without suggesting a rule. 🚫 implies something is officially not permitted. "Wrong answer" calls for ❌; "not allowed here" calls for 🚫.
🚭 is the same red circle and slash with a cigarette inside, so it applies only to smoking. 🚫 is the blank, general-purpose version that you combine with other words or emoji yourself.

avoid: Do not aim 🚫 at a person's idea in a professional discussion, where it reads as a ruling rather than an opinion.
Avoid using it for real safety instructions without words, since a bare symbol does not say what is prohibited.
Do not use it to tell someone they are unwelcome in a group unless you mean to be that blunt.
design: A red ring crossed by a single diagonal bar running from upper left to lower right, with an empty center. It follows the internationally recognized prohibition sign used on public signage. Platforms draw it almost identically. Its original Unicode name is "no entry sign," which is why the shortcode is :no_entry_sign: even though a different emoji, ⛔, depicts the actual no-entry road sign.

faqs.a: It spells "no cap," slang meaning no lie or for real. "Cap" means a lie or exaggeration, and the prohibited sign negates it. People add it after a statement to insist they are being honest.

faqs.q: What does 🚫 mean in a bio?
faqs.a: It introduces something the account owner does not want: "🚫 DMs," "🚫 hate," or "🚫 under 18" are common. It is a boundary notice. What follows the emoji tells you the specific rule.

They overlap but are not identical. 🚫 is the general prohibition sign, while ⛔ copies the road sign for no entry. Confusingly, 🚫 was originally named "no entry sign" in Unicode, so apps sometimes label them in ways that look swapped.

faqs.q: What does 🚫 mean from a girl or guy?
faqs.a: They are refusing something or setting a limit, and the meaning comes from what it is attached to. In flirting it is often playful, as in "🚫 you can't say that." Used alone after a request, it is a clear no.
